TABLE 10.1 Complications and Risks Associated with Anemia in Pregnancy 
Screening for anemia and ID in pregnant clients to improve maternal and infant health outcomes is a secondary 
health promotion intervention. The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (2021) now recommends

screening for anemia in all pregnant clients at the first prenatal visit and, if detected, screening for iron deficiency. 
However, current guidelines do not recommend prepregnancy iron screening. This decreases the chance of early 
identification because individuals may not be aware they are pregnant until later in the pregnancy. 
Iron deficiency and IDA are found equally often among pregnant individuals; however, ID alone doubles in the third
